title: Influence of carbohydrate-electrolyte drinks on marathon running performance
authors: Tsintzas OK, Williams C, Singh R, Wilson W, Burrin J
journal: European Journal of Applied Physiology and Occupational Physiology
population: 7 endurance-trained runners in three randomised 42.2-km treadmill time trials 4 weeks apart (about 190 to 194 min)
findings: The runners drank 3 mL/kg of water, a 6.9% carbohydrate solution or a 5.5% carbohydrate solution before the start and 2 mL/kg every 5 km; total volume was about 1.1 L in each.
Times were 193.9 +/- 5.0 (water), 192.4 +/- 3.3 (6.9%) and 190.0 +/- 3.9 min (5.5%); the 5.5% trial was faster than water (P < 0.05).
Running speed was maintained in the 5.5% trial, whereas it fell after 10 km on water and after 25 km on the 6.9% solution (P < 0.05).
limitations: Seven runners on a treadmill; a 3 h 10 min effort, faster than most recreational marathons but far slower than elite; about 1.1 L of drink in total, so a small dose by current practice; the abstract does not state grams per hour (computing about 60 g in total from volume and concentration is arithmetic, not a stated result); the abstract was truncated by the indexer.
implications: With a small carbohydrate dose, the best-fed arm held speed through a 3 h 10 min marathon-length run and finished about 2% faster than water. Older and small; supports 'some carbohydrate helps in a marathon-length effort' and gives no rate.

verification.notes: Crossref matches (EJAP 70:154-160, 1995). Abstract read on Europe PMC, which truncates it at 250 words ('ABSTRACT TRUNCATED'); findings use only the part shown. Crossref lists no correction, erratum or retraction notice (checked 2026-11-16).
